result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous sidewalk with a grass buffer, though utility poles and signs create physical obstructions in the walkway. A marked crosswalk is present at the side street intersection, but the lack of pedestrian-specific signals and the presence of large parked vehicles obstructing sightlines reduce overall safety.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole and signpost are located directly in the path of the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the accessible width for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicle
hazards.description: A large white truck is parked near the intersection, blocking sightlines between pedestrians at the crosswalk and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway near the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: The signalized intersection lacks dedicated pedestrian walk/don't-walk signals, increasing the risk of crossing conflicts.

interventions.title: Relocate utility poles
interventions.description: Move utility poles and signposts to the furniture zone or buffer strip to ensure a clear, unobstructed walking path.

interventions.title: Implement daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Install pedestrian signals
interventions.description: Add pedestrian countdown signals and push buttons to provide clear guidance and dedicated crossing time.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide residential thoroughfare with four travel lanes and on-street parallel parking. Pedestrian infrastructure includes sidewalks on both sides separated by grass buffers and a signalized intersection with marked crosswalks.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center left, across the main roadway

hazards.name: High-speed road geometry
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes and lack of traffic calming measures encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential area.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island at the crosswalk to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The environment is a typical suburban arterial road with a sidewalk on one side separated by a grass buffer. While a walkway exists, the wide roadway and lack of visible crossing infrastructure create a high-speed, auto-oriented environment that is challenging for pedestrians.

hazards.name: High-speed road design
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes with minimal friction encourage high vehicle speeds adjacent to the pedestrian walkway.

hazards.name: Lack of crossing infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or signals are visible despite residential and commercial land uses on opposite sides of the street.

hazards.name: Driveway conflict points
hazards.description: Vehicle access points to commercial parking lots cross the sidewalk, creating potential conflict zones.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, mid-ground

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility continental markings to provide safe crossing points between residential and commercial areas.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes to encourage slower vehicle speeds and reduce pedestrian crossing distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: If a crossing is installed, include a median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained sidewalk separated from a commercial parking area by a significant grassy embankment. While the physical separation from vehicles is high, the environment is car-centric with a lack of shade, pedestrian-scale lighting, or active street frontage.

hazards.name: Lack of shade
hazards.description: The absence of street trees or structures provides no protection from sun or heat, making the environment uncomfortable for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible sidewalk length

hazards.name: Blank frontage
hazards.description: The large grassy embankment creates a lack of active frontage and natural surveillance, which can impact perceived safety.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees along the buffer would provide shade, reduce the heat island effect, and improve the aesthetic quality of the walk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Adding lighting specifically for the walkway would improve visibility and safety for pedestrians at night.
